prompt: Sort chores by their ISO due date with undated ones last and name as the tie-break, using the two-argument Comparator.comparing with Comparator.nullsLast around natural order.
explanation: The two-argument Comparator.comparing takes a key extractor AND a comparator for the extracted keys, which is the only place a null-tolerant key comparator can be installed; nullsLast(naturalOrder()) treats null as larger than everything so undated chores sink to the bottom. thenComparing(Chore::name) only runs when the first comparator reports a tie, which covers both same-date chores and two undated ones. ISO-8601 dates are zero-padded and ordered largest unit first, so plain String comparison already gives correct chronological order.
hints: Comparator.comparing has a two-argument form: the key extractor, then a comparator for the keys.
Comparator.nullsLast(Comparator.naturalOrder()) is that key comparator -- it sends nulls to the end.
Chain .thenComparing(Chore::name) after it, and sort new ArrayList<>(chores) rather than the parameter.
